what: Stage B4 drive-backoff probe (geometry generalization): uniform (s=1) dolfinx hold-out peak vs drive for the CUBE. The 9000-node rows are the SAME fine arbiter the heavy AL solve reads; the 2500-node rows are a faster bracket used to locate the drive->peak curve (finer 9000 mesh resolves a ~+5.7 C higher peak). Peaks are MEASURED (no false-green).

pick.note: ~0.5 C below band low -> marginally more conservative; a=0.58 would sit mid-band if more throughput is wanted

finding: On the square power-density baseline the cube heats LESS per unit power density, so its feasible drive_a (~0.57) is HIGHER than the square 0.34x, not lower. The S1 281/265 numbers are on the Phase E opener drive scale.
rule: pick the drive whose 9000-node uniform peak is a few C UNDER T_eff=235, leaving room to shape UP toward 235 while staying feasible vs the real 250 ceiling
